north_star.fact: Tool ARGUMENTS and RESULTS reach aws/spans as span ATTRIBUTES — attributes.gen_ai.tool.call.arguments and .result — but ONLY on `mcp tools/call <target>___<tool>` spans, emitted by the AgentCore MCP client instrumentation and flagged telemetry.extended=true. Strands-level `execute_tool <name>` spans (our own builtins) carry NEITHER — only gen_ai.tool.json_schema (the tool's SCHEMA, not the call) plus description and status. span events[] is ALWAYS empty: the exporter drops the OTel events that Strands emits, which is why the code-only reading concluded "events, never attributes". Coverage measured 2,416 of 6,518 TOOL spans over 14 days (~37%), and 718 argument-bearing records in a 3-day window. Consequence unchanged and now sharper — span data is SENSITIVE-DATA-BEARING (real arguments and result bodies), so redaction/retention/access are first-class, and compliance.RedactingLogWriter still has ZERO callers (OURS-4).
north_star.practical_rule: Query the named attributes directly. Do NOT use `fields @message` for volume work (events are empty, records are large), and do NOT use `fields attributes.*` as the original harvest did — that is what produced the false negative.
north_star.wrong_previously: "emitted as OTEL span *events* (gen_ai.tool.message), never as span *attributes*" — derived from Strands source alone. The live check refuted it: the MCP instrumentation writes attributes via a different code path. The harvest's real miss was projecting a fields list that named neither.
